claim: The two components of structural uncertainty—across-trial ranking instability and within-trial candidate ambiguity—relate oppositely to reasoning accuracy: within-trial ambiguity correlates positively with correctness on reasoning tasks, while across-trial instability correlates negatively.
falsifier: On a new set of reasoning tasks, compute the correlation of each component with accuracy: within-trial ambiguity should show a positive correlation, across-trial instability a negative correlation, replicating the opposite-sign pattern.

exclusions: limited to the five LLMs and eight benchmarks studied; transfer beyond these systems and tasks is unestablished

title: Across-trial ranking instability–reasoning accuracy principle

claim: Training video LLMs on pseudo videos (generated by repeating images with mild affine transformations) yields temporal reasoning performance close to, and occasionally higher than, training on real videos.
falsifier: Train a video LLM on pseudo videos created by repeating images with mild affine transformations and evaluate its temporal reasoning on TVBench; compare performance to a version trained on real videos. The pseudo-video-trained model should perform similarly or better.

conditions: Pseudo videos are generated by repeating a single image with mild affine transformations per frame
Evaluation is performed on TVBench, a benchmark designed to require temporal reasoning
Models are otherwise trained with the same procedure
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the specific pseudo video generation method and the two Video LLMs studied; transfer to other generation methods, models, or benchmarks is unestablished

title: Training data type: pseudo–Temporal reasoning performance on principle
